gaps.discriminates: A definitive sonographic finding of retroplacental clot would confirm abruption; absence does not exclude it, but combined with normal fibrinogen and lack of clinical deterioration would favor alternatives like previa or local trauma

gaps.info: Detailed uterine activity tracing (e.g., frequency, intensity, resting tone) and maternal vital signs trend (BP, HR, perfusion markers)
gaps.discriminates: Sustained high uterine resting tone (>20 mmHg) or tetanic contractions support abruption; hypotension/tachycardia would heighten concern for concealed hemorrhage or rupture, while stable vitals with isolated decels may favor cord compression or previa
